claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out about claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 4 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'm happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few more questions:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care, such as paying for food, clothes, and his general upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I take care of all his needs - his food, clothes, everything he needs day to day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful, thank you for confirming that.

Now, could you tell me a bit about your own situation – are you a UK resident, and do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, as a British citizen, settled status, or another form of immigration permission)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester actually, and yes, I have the right to be here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions – is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

Is Alex in full-time education, or is he currently just at home or in nursery/preschool given his age (4 years old)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's just 4, so he's not in full-time school yet. He goes to nursery a few days a week, but nothing formal like primary school yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK and have the right to be here
- Alex is 4 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care (food, clothes, etc.)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

I'm pleased to say that you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me record this outcome for you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **Alex is under 16** – at 4 years old, he meets the age requirement
✅ **You live in the UK** – and have the right to reside here
✅ **Alex lives with you** – so you meet the responsibility requirement
✅ **You're responsible for his care** – providing his food, clothes and day-to-day needs
✅ **No one else is claiming** – only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child

You can apply for Child Benefit online through the official government website, or by post using the Child Benefit claim form. If you have any other questions about the application process, feel free to ask!
